subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which character represents the Church through promises of "Sugarcandy Mountain"?
questions.explain: Moses the raven preaches of a paradise called Sugarcandy Mountain, satirising how religion can pacify the oppressed.

questions.q: What happens to the windmill the first time the animals complete it?
options: It is destroyed in a storm, which Napoleon blames on Snowball
questions.explain: A storm topples the windmill, and Napoleon scapegoats the exiled Snowball to deflect blame.

questions.q: Which two pigs become rivals for leadership after the Rebellion?
questions.explain: Napoleon and Snowball compete for control until Napoleon drives Snowball out.

questions.q: Which Victorian theory, holding that helping the poor only increased their numbers, does Scrooge's early attitude echo?
questions.explain: Scrooge's line about "decrease the surplus population" reflects Malthusian thinking Dickens criticised.

questions.q: What does Marley's ghost wear that symbolises a life devoted to greed?
options: A chain of cash-boxes, keys and ledgers
questions.explain: His chain is made of "cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers", the heavy weight of his earthly avarice.

questions.q: In a poem, 'enjambment' is when a line runs on into the next without end-stop punctuation. What effect can this create?
options: A fixed, regular beat in every line
A repeated sound at the end of lines
A sense of momentum, flow or breathlessness that mirrors meaning
A pause in the middle of a line
questions.explain: Enjambment carries sense over the line break, often creating flow, urgency or a spilling-over effect that can reflect the poem's content.

questions.q: Why might a writer use 'foreshadowing'?
options: To hint at events to come, building tension or a sense of inevitability
To confuse the reader about the genre
questions.explain: Foreshadowing plants clues about later events, creating suspense or a feeling that an outcome is unavoidable.

questions.q: 'Juxtaposition' is a technique in which a writer...
options: Places two contrasting ideas or images close together for effect
Repeats the same word three times
questions.explain: Juxtaposition sets contrasting elements side by side to highlight differences and provoke thought.

questions.q: What broader social concern does Dickens press through the figures of Ignorance and Want?
options: Society's neglect of poor children and the need for education and care
questions.explain: Dickens warns that neglecting poor children, especially through ignorance, breeds doom unless society takes responsibility.

questions.q: What ultimately happens to Boxer when he collapses from overwork?
options: He is sold to a knacker to be slaughtered
He is sent to a peaceful retirement
questions.explain: Napoleon sells the loyal Boxer to the knacker for money, despite claiming he was sent to a vet.

questions.q: The 'protagonist' of a text is...
options: The central character whose journey drives the narrative
The character who opposes the hero
questions.explain: The protagonist is the main character at the centre of the action, often in conflict with an antagonist.

questions.q: Despite their poverty, how does Bob Cratchit respond to Scrooge during the Christmas toast?
options: He insists on toasting Scrooge as the founder of the feast
questions.explain: Bob generously toasts Scrooge as "the Founder of the Feast", revealing the Cratchits' warmth despite Scrooge's cruelty.

questions.q: How does a 'soliloquy' differ from an 'aside'?
options: They are identical in every way
An aside is always longer than a soliloquy
An aside can only be spoken by the protagonist
A soliloquy is delivered alone; an aside is a brief remark while others are on stage
questions.explain: An aside is a quick comment heard only by the audience while other characters remain on stage, whereas a soliloquy is spoken when the character is alone.

questions.q: How does Napoleon finally seize sole power over the farm?
options: He sets his trained dogs on Snowball to chase him away
questions.explain: Napoleon unleashes the fierce dogs he reared in secret to expel Snowball.

questions.q: A 'symbol' in literature is best described as...
options: A word that rhymes with another
The main character of a story
An object, image or action that stands for a larger idea
A pause in the middle of a line
questions.explain: A symbol carries meaning beyond its literal self, representing an abstract idea such as hope, death or freedom.

questions.q: A 'sonnet' is most reliably identified by which feature?
options: Fourteen lines, usually in iambic pentameter, with a structured rhyme scheme
A refrain repeated after every stanza
Exactly three stanzas of six lines
questions.explain: The fourteen-line structure with a regular rhyme scheme and a turn is the hallmark of the sonnet form.

questions.q: How does Dickens use Fred to challenge Scrooge's view of Christmas and the poor?
options: Fred argues Christmas is a kind, charitable time and keeps offering Scrooge warmth
questions.explain: Fred insists Christmas is a good, generous time and repeatedly extends warmth to Scrooge, embodying the spirit of goodwill.

questions.q: Which pig acts as Napoleon's propagandist, persuading the animals to accept his decisions?
questions.explain: Squealer twists facts and rewrites events to justify Napoleon's rule.

questions.q: What was the name of Scrooge's kind former employer, who is shown hosting a joyful Christmas party?
questions.explain: Old Fezziwig, Scrooge's generous master, throws a warm Christmas party that contrasts with Scrooge's own meanness.

questions.q: What does Dickens use the Cratchit family to highlight about Victorian society?
options: The dignity and hardship of the working poor
questions.explain: The loving but struggling Cratchits dramatise poverty and the case for social responsibility.

questions.q: Who does the pig Squealer represent as he spreads Napoleon's propaganda in Animal Farm?
questions.explain: Squealer is an allegory for Stalinist propaganda that manipulates the other animals.

questions.q: Who is Bob Cratchit?
questions.explain: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's poorly paid, overworked but warm-hearted clerk.
